title: Holm Oak: Ancient Evergreen Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: The oak that never loses its leaves, dark, domed and drought-proof. The oldest holm oaks mapped so far, from Mediterranean parks to Atlantic gardens.
intro: The holm oak is the oak most northern visitors fail to recognise: evergreen, with small dark leathery leaves closer to an olive's than to the lobed oak leaf on every pub sign, holly-like enough that holm is simply the old English word for holly. Around the Mediterranean it is the landscape itself, the dark domed canopy of Spanish dehesas where pigs fatten on its acorns for jamon iberico, and it shrugs off drought, salt wind and poor soil that would kill its deciduous cousins. Planted north of its range it grows slowly into dense, near-black domes that read as older than they are. The holm oaks mapped so far are listed oldest first.
